transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I've been trying to get people to understand this for months now. My husband's family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It's just obvious to me. Like, little billing errors will suddenly show up at my work, or someone at church will start acting really funny toward me for no reason. People try to pull up records or paperwork to tell me I'm wrong, but no matter what they show me, I know it all ties back to his family. I just need someone to actually see what's happening.
Do you think other people believe his family is behind these events as well?

No, they don't. That's the problem. Whenever I try to explain it to anyone—my husband, my friends, my boss—they just look at me like I'm crazy. They tell me it's just a coincidence or a mistake, or that I'm overthinking it. But I'm not. I just don't know how to make them see it.
Have you ever seen or heard things that other people couldn't?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I know what you're asking, but no. 

The things I'm talking about—the billing errors at work, the paperwork—they are real things right there on a computer screen or on a desk. Anyone can physically see them. It's just the... the actual reason behind them that people refuse to see.
How long have you been noticing these events that you believe are connected to your husband's family?

It's been about nine months now. Yeah, right around nine months. It all started right after we had some trouble with his family over money, and... well, holiday expectations. Ever since that happened, that's when all these things just started popping up.
Have you ever considered the possibility that his family might not be behind these events?

I mean... I've tried to think maybe I'm wrong, just because of how everyone else reacts. But I can't. I’m here because for months now, I’ve just been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It's happening right in front of me. Like when those little billing errors show up at work, or... or when someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me out of nowhere. People tell me it's nothing, or they try to show me proof that it's a mistake, but no matter what records anyone pulls up, I know it ties back to them. I just know it.
Do you think there's something wrong with your mind or your thinking?

No, I don't. I mean, my mind is fine. I'm thinking clearly. I know people probably think I'm crazy because of how much I talk about it, but... I'm just putting the pieces together. My memory is good, I do my job well, I pay my bills. There's nothing wrong with my brain. It's just that I'm the only one willing to look at what's actually happening.
Can you think of any other possible explanation for the billing errors and the strange behavior from people at church, other than your husband's family being involved?

Honestly... no. I really can't. Like I was just saying, I know people want there to be another explanation. They pull up the billing records at work and try to tell me it's just a typo, or they say the people at church are just busy and didn't mean to act strange toward me. 

But I know what's actually happening. I've been trying to get someone to understand this for months. It's his family. They are quietly messing with our money and our reputation, and no matter what paperwork anyone tries to show me to prove otherwise, I know for a fact it all ties back to them.
Do you think it's possible that you might be wrong about his family being behind these events?

I feel like we keep going in circles with this, doctor. Like I just said... no. I don't think I'm wrong. 

I know I keep repeating myself, but I've been dealing with this for months, just trying to get people to understand what's happening. My husband's family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. I see it when those little billing errors show up at my job, and I see it when people at church suddenly act funny toward me out of nowhere. Everyone else wants to pull up records and make excuses for it, but I know it ties back to them. I'm completely sure of it.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about your husband's family is something that you might be misinterpreting or misunderstanding?

No, I don't think I'm misunderstanding anything. I mean, we've talked about this... I know what I'm seeing. 

I'm here because I've spent months trying to get someone, anyone, to understand what his family is doing. They are quietly messing with our money and our good name. It's not a misunderstanding when those little billing errors keep showing up at my work. It's not a misinterpretation when people at church suddenly act funny toward me. 

People can pull up whatever records they want to try and prove me wrong, but I know the truth. It all ties back to his family. I'm not misinterpreting it, I'm just the only one seeing it for what it is.
How have you been feeling emotionally over the past nine months while dealing with these situations?

I don't know... just frustrated, mostly. I haven't really stopped to think about my emotions, to be honest. 

It's just stressful. You know, dealing with all this and feeling like you're hitting a brick wall when you try to explain it to people. But I'm still going to work, doing my job, and taking care of what I need to take care of. I wouldn't say I'm feeling anything out of the ordinary, really. Just... tired of the whole situation, I guess.
How would you describe your relationship with your husband?

Well, it's been a bit strained lately. We've definitely had more arguments because of all this. He thinks I should just let it go, and it's the same with some people at church—there have been some awkward moments because they think I should just drop it, too. 

But it's not like my whole life is falling apart. I haven't lost my job, and I'm still taking care of all my usual responsibilities at home and at work. It's just... the arguments with him are getting tiring.
Have you considered that your belief about your husband's family might be interfering with other aspects of your life?

Not really, no. Like I said, it's not ruining my life or anything. I still get up every morning for work. I handle all my billing clerk duties just fine... I keep the house going, make sure everything is taken care of. I even still have time for myself, you know, I spend time out in the garden or doing a little painting. 

So, no, it's not interfering with my day-to-day stuff. The only time... well, the main trouble really just comes up when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing. That's when the pushback and the arguments happen. But the rest of my life is completely normal.
Have you been feeling anxious about the situation with your husband's family?

Not really anxious, no. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying or feeling nervous all day. I know exactly what they're doing, so there's no mystery to be anxious over. It's really just... aggravating, having to deal with it and having people push back when I bring it up. But I wouldn't say I have anxiety about it.
Do you think that people are talking about you or your situation when you're not around?

No, I don't really think so. I mean, I don't get the feeling that people are whispering behind my back or anything like that. When they have an issue with what I'm saying, they usually just tell me to my face. Like my husband or the folks at church, they just tell me I need to let it go. So, no, I don't think there's any secret talking going on when I'm not in the room.
Was there anything unusual or stressful happening in your life right before you first started noticing these events with your husband's family?

Well, it all started about nine months ago. There wasn't really anything unusual going on, just... a lot of trouble with my husband's family. We were having disagreements over money and, you know, what they expected from us for the holidays. That's when I first started noticing what they were really up to. So, yeah, it's been going on for about nine months now, ever since that whole situation.
Have you ever had a similar belief or concern about someone or something else before your husband's family?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've never really had a reason to. Before all this started with his family, everything was pretty normal. I just went to work, came home... I've never dealt with anyone doing things like this to me before, so no, nothing like this in the past.
How much time would you say you spend thinking about your husband's family and their supposed actions against you on a typical day?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't... I don't track the hours or anything like that. It's just on my mind when I have to deal with them or when something comes up. But as for an actual amount of time during a typical day, I really couldn't say.
Do you think any amount of proof or evidence could change your mind about your husband's family being behind these events?

Honestly, no. I don't think so. I’ve been trying to get people to understand this for months now. My husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name, and I know it's them. It's things like... little billing errors showing up at my work, or someone at church suddenly acting funny toward me out of nowhere. People try to tell me I'm wrong, but no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and prove it's just a coincidence, I know it ties back to them. So, no, a piece of paper or some evidence wouldn't change my mind because I already know what they're doing.
